name: mmix
desc: 64-bit RISC architecture designed by Donald Knuth
why: Knuth's 64-bit RISC teaching machine with its own assembler and simulator, a delightful door into how computers really execute.

brief.what_it_is: MMIX is a 64-bit RISC machine designed by Donald Knuth, described on this site as a teaching architecture that is easy to learn yet representative of modern machines. MMIXware is the software package around it: an assembler (mmixal) and a simulator (mmix), plus related tools. You feed it MMIX assembly source and run it on the simulator, which executes the program on the emulated machine. The homepage names the assembler and simulator but does not describe the other installed executables (mmmix, mmotype) in any detail.
brief.why_it_exists: Knuth designed MMIX to replace the MIX machine in the published volumes 1 to 3 of The Art of Computer Programming and to use it in later volumes, starting with volume 4. The MMIX Supplement provides MMIX versions of every MIX program in those volumes.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internal mechanism of the simulator or assembler beyond saying that MMIXware, as described in Volume 1 Fascicle 1 of TAOCP, was frozen in September 2011. The MMIXware book, a Lecture Notes in Computer Science volume, documents Version 1 of the architecture and corresponds to the mmix-20131017.tgz release.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists prebuilt executables for Win32, Linux 32-bit and Mac OS X, and says the sources are in a git repository at https://gitlab.lrz.de/mmix. It also mentions MMIXVD, a Windows-only visual debugger and IDE that bundles an editor, mmixal and mmix. A Java IDE by Anselm Binninger (BWK-Technik) is linked. No accounts, runtimes or configuration steps are mentioned on the homepage. The Homebrew formula supplies the four executables directly.
brief.standout: Knuth designed a whole machine, instruction set and toolchain for teaching, and the software is a frozen, bug-free-by-definition reference rather than a moving project. The software is tied to a published book and to the TAOCP series, so it reads as a companion to Knuth's text rather than a standalone tool.
brief.status: Mixed. The homepage says MMIXware Version 1 was frozen in September 2011 and is 'permanently frozen', with the last named tarball dated 2013 (mmix-20131017.tgz). The site says it 'coordinates the future development of MMIXware' and mentions a new MMIXVD 1.1 release, but gives no dates for it. Overall: the core is frozen and the site is maintained as a reference hub; recent software activity is unknown.
brief.caveats: Version 1 of the architecture is frozen, so no new features are expected in the core. The Linux binaries are 32-bit only. MMIXVD is Windows-only. Much of the documentation is in PDF. The homepage itself lists no commands and no quick-start steps; those are on the Getting Started page, which I did not reach because the homepage did not expose its link targets to me.
quotes: Welcome to all lovers of clean (or nearly clean) hardware design!
A RISC computer for the new millennium
Version 1 is permanently frozen, and "bug-free by definition."
